title: Display switcher, filter and Search icons match the design in every display
custom_preconds:
Setup file (for Claude sessions; a tester does not need it)

Preconditions

  • You are signed in as an Admin user (the "Admin" role, which has Work orders > View and Create & Edit) at {Location-A}.
    For example: {Location-A} is Staging Heavy Duty - 9919.
  • The browser window is 1440 px wide with the zoom at 100%, and the design pictures "DC-01-toolbar-tech-view-light-1440.png" and "DC-01-toolbar-board-view-light-1440.png" attached to this case are open beside it at 100% (actual size). Names, numbers and rank numbers in the pictures are sample data.
  • Customer {Customer-A} has one Approved work order, {Work-order-1}, led by technician {Technician-A}.
    For example: {Customer-A} is ZZAUTOTEST C590110 Toolbar Icons, {Work-order-1} is S10043-17801 and {Technician-A} is ZZAUTOTEST C590110 Ana.
  • Starting screen: "Work Orders" > "All" tab, "List" shown, "Search" empty, no filter chosen, "Assigned to me" off, density "Regular".
  • If any record above is missing, mark this test Blocked: "setup not done".
custom_steps:
1. On the "Work Orders" page, look at the three buttons of the display switcher.
  2. Look at the icon in "Search" and the icons on "Status", "Assigned to me" and "Asset on Site".
  3. Click "Tech View" in the display switcher.
  4. Look at the density button and the "Column Selection" button.
  5. Look at the icon in "Search" and the filter icons.
  6. Click the density button.
  7. Click "Board View" in the display switcher.
  8. Look at the density button.
  9. Look at the icon in "Search" and the filter icons.
  10. Click "List" in the display switcher.
custom_expected:
Expected results

  • Step 1: three thin outline icons side by side in a light-grey rounded track (a bulleted list, the head and shoulders of a person, a square board with three bars), the same drawings and size as in the design pictures, drawn in the same slate grey as in the pictures.
  • Step 2: a magnifier in Search; on the filters a circle of short strokes (Status), a clipboard with lines (Assigned to me) and a truck (Asset on Site), thin outlines as in the design picture.
  • Step 3: the Tech View button sits on a white raised segment, the other two look flat, and the switcher icons keep the same slate grey as in List.
  • Step 4: the density button shows three lines with an up-and-down arrow and the Column Selection button a rectangle split into three columns, thin slate outlines as in the Tech View picture.
  • Step 5: the same Search and filter icons as in List at step 2.
  • Step 6: the density menu offers "Compact", "Regular" and "Comfortable", with "Regular" marked as in use.
  • Step 7: the Board View button is now the white raised segment and the switcher icons keep the same slate grey.
  • Step 8: the density button shows a card with an up-and-down arrow, as in the Board View picture.
  • Step 9: the same Search and filter icons as in List at step 2.
  • Step 10: apart from the Search and filter icons and the display switcher, List's toolbar icons look as they do in production today.

Source — where this behaviour comes from
Epic SV-10043; stories SV-10044 (Story 1, Switch between display options), SV-10049 (Story 6, Density); PRD "Work Orders — Board View & Tech View Display Options", Confluence 845185030, version 61 (16 Oct 2026, Chris Ward), S1-R9a, S2-R23, S1-R9, S6-R1 and Goals, read 16 Oct 2026. Claude Design project "Work Orders" (Branko Cicovic), export of 14 Oct 2026, board "Work Orders.dc.html" (the design pictures named in the preconditions were rendered from it), read 14 Oct 2026. Related tickets: SV-11319. Product owner answers: Chris Ward, WO Board and Tech View question sheet (https://docs.google.com/spreadsheets/d/1gBGmNB4B1bRrD2ZJvBn1tuvbfxFPjcsKddz_I5H3CvU), answers 12, 21 and 24, read 15 Oct 2026. Source-verified 16 October 2026. Last checked against build v26.40.19-1493c63 (staging) on 10/16/2026.

Until 15 Oct 2026 the PRD (version 52) left every List icon unchanged, so this case did not judge the filter icons. Chris Ward answered on 15 Oct 2026 (answer 12) that the filter chips and Search use the design file's icons in every display option, List included, and (answer 21) that today's tabs, toolbar and Create Work Order button stay. PRD versions 54 to 61 say so, and this case follows them. The design names the three options Table, By Lead Tech and Board; PRD version 61 still keeps List, Tech View and Board View (answer 24). The Technician filter's wrench icon is checked in the Technician filter design case.

PRD versions 55 and 58 (S1-R9a, S2-R23; Chris Ward rulings on Slavcho Mitrov's questions and PR notes, 15 Oct 2026) add that the display switcher's icons and the toolbar icons are the design's slate colour in every view, List included; steps 1, 3, 4 and 7 check it.

Exact quotes from the source (for reproducibility)

  • S1-R9a: “The switcher uses the design’s icons at 20px: List is Lucide `list`, Tech View is `user-round`, Board View is `square-kanban`. In Tech View and Board View these icons are the design’s: density (`row-height` in Tech View, `card-height` in Board View, custom icons in the design system’s icon set), collapse chevron (`chevron-down`), pin and unpin (`pin` / `pin-off`), Invoiced or Paid lock (`lock`), Unassigned avatar (`user-round`) and the empty state when there are no work orders at all (`clipboard-list`). The filtered no-results state is the List’s, magnifier included (S1-N1). The filter chips and Search use the design file’s icons in every display option, List included, each exactly as the design file draws it. The display switcher (new on every view, List included) shows the design’s slate icons in every view, so it keeps one color as the user moves between views. These are the only changes to List. Every other List icon is unchanged.”
  • S2-R23: “In Tech View and Board View, as in the design: a technician avatar without a photo is a light-grey circle (--sv-grey-100, #EEF2F6) with initials in --sv-grey-600 (#4B5565) in light mode, which meets accessible contrast (6.7:1; the design file’s #697586 is 4.2:1); dark mode uses the design’s dark colors; group and column header names are 14px, weight 600, in the design’s slate text color (#364152), with the design’s smaller, lighter initials; Board card customer and total price are weight 500; toolbar and switcher icons are the design’s slate color (the switcher in List too, S1-R9a). Technician avatars, and the Service Advisor avatar, follow density in Tech View as in the design: 20px, 24px and 32px on rows and 24px, 28px and 36px on group headers at Compact, Regular and Comfortable; Board View card avatars stay 24px. The Progress bar is 48 by 4px at Compact, as in the design. The name bubble on hover over a technician avatar on a row or card (the +N included) opens above the avatar, in both views; group and column header avatars keep the browser’s plain name tip, because the name is printed beside them. In Tech View, Status, Waiting On Parts and Progress are left-aligned. The Density and Columns tooltips open above their button, like the switcher’s (S1-R9b), and are hidden while their menu is open. List is unchanged.”
  • S1-R9: “The switcher visually indicates the active display option.”
  • S6-R1: “Offer Compact, Regular, and Comfortable density in Tech View and Board View.”
  • Goals: “List remains the default and is unchanged from production. The only changes to the Work Orders page are the display switcher and the icons on the filter chips and Search, which follow the design file in every display option, List included (S1-R9a). Today’s tabs, toolbar layout and Create Work Order button stay as they are.”
  • Design — _ds_bundle.js (design library), density button icon: “name: kanban ? 'card-height' : 'row-height',”
  • Design — _ds_bundle.js (design library), column chooser button icon: “window.svIcon("columns-3", 20)”
  • Design — README.md (design library), icons: “Never emoji. Never a unicode glyph as an icon.”
  • Design — _ds_bundle.js (design library), Work Orders filter chip Status icon: “id: "status", icon: SVIcons.ICON_LOAD, label: "Status",”
  • Design — _ds_bundle.js (design library), Work Orders filter chip Assigned to me icon: “id: "mine", icon: svGlyph("clipboard-list", 16), label: "Assigned to me",”
  • Design — _ds_bundle.js (design library), Work Orders filter chip Asset on site icon: “id: "asset", icon: SVIcons.ICON_TRUCK, label: "Asset on site",”
  • Design — _ds_bundle.js (design library), spinner icon: “ICON_LOAD: lazyGlyph("loader"),”
  • Design — _ds_bundle.js (design library), Search icon: “ICON_SEARCH: lazyGlyph("search", 20),”

title: Switcher tooltips read List, Tech View, Board View and open above it
custom_preconds:
Setup (manual QA tester and Claude session)

Preconditions

  • You are signed in as {User-A} (for example Admin ShopView), an Owner or Admin user whose role has Work orders > View, Work orders > Create & Edit and See financial data, at {Location-A} (for example Staging Heavy Duty - 9919).
  • Your browser window is 1440 px wide, with the browser zoom at 100%.
  • For the steps that name 1536 px, your screen lets you widen the window to 1536 px.
  • The design picture DC-02-tech-view-header-row-1440.png is open beside the app at 100% zoom (actual size); it is attached to this case.
  • The design picture shows the column header row that must stay readable; the design has no tooltip of its own on the switcher, so where the tooltip opens comes from the PRD.
  • Technician {Technician-A} (for example ZZAUTOTEST DC02 Ben Tooltip) is an active technician at {Location-A}.
  • Customer {Customer-A} (for example "ZZAUTOTEST DC02 Switcher Tooltip") is used by this case only.
  • Approved work order {Work-order-1} (for example S10043-17805) for {Customer-A} is led by {Technician-A}.
  • On the Work Orders page nothing is chosen in any filter (if the Asset on Site chip shows Yes or No, click the x on the chip), Assigned to me is off, Search is empty and density is Regular (the default).
custom_steps:
1. Open Work Orders, click the All tab and click Tech View in the display switcher.
  2. Hover the List button of the display switcher and wait until its tooltip shows.
  3. Hover the Tech View button and wait until its tooltip shows.
  4. Hover the Board View button and wait until its tooltip shows.
  5. Click Board View in the display switcher.
  6. Hover each of the three switcher buttons in turn, waiting for each tooltip.
  7. Widen the window to 1536 px.
  8. Click Tech View in the display switcher.
  9. Hover each of the three switcher buttons in turn, waiting for each tooltip.
custom_expected:
Expected results

  • Steps 2 to 4: each tooltip opens above the switcher, between the switcher and the tabs above it, never below it. While it shows, the table's column header row (Status, Waiting On Parts, Number …) stays fully readable, as in the design picture: no part of the tooltip lies over it. The tooltips read List (step 2), Tech View (step 3) and Board View (step 4).
  • Step 6: in Board View each tooltip also opens above the switcher, reads List, Tech View or Board View, and covers none of the column headers (technician names and counts).
  • Step 9: at 1536 px each tooltip still opens above the switcher and leaves the column header row fully readable.

Source — where this behaviour comes from
Epic SV-10043; story SV-10044 (Story 1, Switch between display options); PRD "Work Orders — Board View & Tech View Display Options", Confluence 845185030, version 54 (15 Oct 2026, Chris Ward), S1-R9b and S1-R1, read 15 Oct 2026; Claude Design project "Work Orders" (Branko Cicovic), export of 14 Oct 2026, board "Work Orders.dc.html", state core__work-orders__tech-regular__light__1440 (design pictures DC-02-tech-view-header-row-1440.png, rendered from that export at the width in the name), read 14 Oct 2026. Covers the design defects SV-11322 (reported 14 Oct 2026 by Chris Ward). Where the PRD says nothing about the look, the design is the source. Product owner answers: Chris Ward, WO Board and Tech View question sheet (https://docs.google.com/spreadsheets/d/1gBGmNB4B1bRrD2ZJvBn1tuvbfxFPjcsKddz_I5H3CvU), answer 24, read 15 Oct 2026. Source-verified 15 October 2026. Last checked against build v26.40.19-72f4f3b (staging) on 10/16/2026.

The design shows only the browser's own hover text on the switcher (Table, By Lead Tech, Board). Chris Ward answered on 15 Oct 2026 (answer 24) that the tooltips read List, Tech View and Board View; PRD version 54 says so, and this case now checks the words as well as the position.

title: Tech View table runs edge to edge on white and the Status column fits its pills

Preconditions

  • You are signed in as an Admin user (the "Admin" role, which has Work orders > View and Create & Edit) at {Location-A}.
    For example: {Location-A} is Staging Heavy Duty - 9919.
  • The browser window is 1440 px wide with the zoom at 100%, and the design pictures "DC-03-tech-view-regular-light-1440.png" and "DC-03-tech-view-regular-light-1536.png" attached to this case are open beside it at 100% (actual size). Names, numbers and rank numbers in the pictures are sample data. Your screen lets you widen the window to 1536 px.
  • Customer {Customer-A} has an Approved work order {Work-order-1}, led by technician {Technician-A}, and an Estimate {Work-order-2} with no lead technician. Customer {Customer-B} has a work order {Work-order-3} in "Ready For Review", led by {Technician-A}.

  • Starting screen: "Work Orders" > "All" tab, "Tech View" shown, "Search" empty, no filter chosen, "Assigned to me" off, density "Regular".
  • If any record above is missing, mark this test Blocked: "setup not done".
custom_steps:
1. Look at the left and right edges of the table, from the column header row down to the last row on screen.
  2. Look at the line between the "Unassigned" group and the next group.
  3. Scroll the table down a few screens.
  4. Scroll the table sideways to its far right.
  5. Widen the window to 1536 px.
  6. Type the name of {Customer-A} in "Search".
  7. Replace the search text with the name of {Customer-B}.
  8. Click "List" in the display switcher.
custom_expected:
Expected results

  • Step 1: the table is white and runs from the page's left edge to its right edge, with no grey strip, margin, card, panel, rounded corner or shadow around it, as in the 1440 px picture.
  • Step 2: the groups are separated by a double grey line above each group header, as in the picture.
  • Step 3: the column header row stays at the top while the rows move up under it.
  • Step 4: the table scrolls sideways inside the page, each header label stays above its own column, and no column is squeezed or cut off.
  • Step 5: at 1536 px the table still runs edge to edge on white, as in the 1536 px picture.
  • Step 6: the "Status" column is only as wide as its widest pill ("Approved" or "Estimate"), with no wide empty space after the pills.
  • Step 7: the "Status" column is wider, just wide enough for the "Ready For Review" pill (about 132 px, as in the design).
  • Step 8: List's table looks as it does in production today.

Source — where this behaviour comes from
Epic SV-10043; story SV-10045 (Story 2, Tech View); PRD "Work Orders — Board View & Tech View Display Options", Confluence 845185030, version 61 (16 Oct 2026, Chris Ward), S2-R22, S2-R1 and Goals, read 16 Oct 2026. title: Tech View opens on 13 default columns with small grey header labels
custom_preconds:
Setup file (for Claude sessions; a tester does not need it)

Preconditions

  • You are signed in with the "Admin" role at {Location-A}, and you have never changed Tech View's columns.
    For example: {Location-A} is Staging Heavy Duty - 9919.
  • The browser window is 1440 px wide with the zoom at 100%, and the design pictures "DC-04-tech-view-header-row-1440.png" and "DC-04-tech-view-all-columns-1440.png" attached to this case are open beside it at 100% (actual size). Names, numbers and rank numbers in the pictures are sample data. Your screen lets you widen the window to 1536 px.
  • Customer {Customer-A} has an Approved work order {Work-order-1}, led by technician {Technician-A}.
    For example: {Customer-A} is ZZAUTOTEST C590113 Columns, {Work-order-1} is S10043-17840 and {Technician-A} is ZZAUTOTEST C590113 Ana.
  • Starting screen: "Work Orders" > "All" tab, "Tech View" shown, the name of {Customer-A} in "Search", no filter chosen, "Assigned to me" off, density "Regular".
  • If any record above is missing, mark this test Blocked: "setup not done".
custom_steps:
1. Read the column header labels from left to right, scrolling the table sideways to see them all.
  2. Compare the size, weight and colour of the header labels with the row text under them and with the design picture.
  3. Look at the space between each pair of neighbouring header labels.
  4. Click the "Column Selection" button.
  5. Turn on "On Site", "VIN/Serial #", "Lead Technician" and every other column the list offers that is off.
  6. Press Escape.
  7. Scroll the table sideways from left to right and look at every header label.
  8. Click the density button and choose "Compact".
  9. Click the density button and choose "Comfortable".
  10. Widen the window to 1536 px.
custom_expected:
Expected results

  • Step 1: 13 columns, in this order: "Status", "Waiting On Parts", "Number", "Customer", "Unit", "Asset", "Progress", "Service Advisor", "Clocked In", "Lines", "Assigned Techs", "Created on", "Total price". "On Site", "VIN/Serial #" and "Lead Technician" are not shown.
  • Step 2: the header labels are small (12 px in the design, smaller than the 14 px row text), medium weight (not bold) and grey (lighter than the row text), as in the picture.
  • Step 3: no header label touches or overlaps its neighbour.
  • Step 4: the column list opens and offers "On Site", "VIN/Serial #" and "Lead Technician".
  • Step 5: each one turned on shows as a column.
  • Step 6: the column list closes.
  • Step 7: with every column on, no header label touches, overlaps or is cut off by its neighbour, as in the all-columns picture.
  • Step 8: the header labels keep the same size, weight and grey colour at Compact.
  • Step 9: the header labels keep the same size, weight and grey colour at Comfortable.
  • Step 10: at 1536 px no header label touches or overlaps its neighbour.

Source — where this behaviour comes from
Epic SV-10043; stories SV-10048 (Story 5, Choose what is shown), SV-10050 (Story 7, Line technicians), SV-10045 (Story 2, Tech View); PRD "Work Orders — Board View & Tech View Display Options", Confluence 845185030, version 61 (16 Oct 2026, Chris Ward), S5-R4, S7-R7, S2-R21 and Out of Scope, read 16 Oct 2026. Claude Design project "Work Orders" (Branko Cicovic), export of 14 Oct 2026, board "Work Orders.dc.html" (the design pictures named in the preconditions were rendered from it), read 14 Oct 2026. Related tickets: SV-11317, SV-11321. Product owner answers: Chris Ward, WO Board and Tech View question sheet (https://docs.google.com/spreadsheets/d/1gBGmNB4B1bRrD2ZJvBn1tuvbfxFPjcsKddz_I5H3CvU), answers 14 and 25, read 15 Oct 2026. Source-verified 16 October 2026. Last checked against build v26.40.17-a5c4210 (staging) on 10/15/2026.

The design's header row reads "Unit #" and "Assigned Tech"; Chris Ward answered on 15 Oct 2026 (answer 14) that the headings are Unit and Assigned Techs, and PRD version 61 still says so. The design's Tech View column chooser does not offer On Site, VIN/Serial # or Lead Technician; PRD version 61 still keeps them as columns that can be added, and this case follows the PRD. title: Tech View cells show a blue number, a thin progress bar and the advisor's avatar
custom_preconds:
Setup file (for Claude sessions; a tester does not need it)

Preconditions

  • You are signed in as an Admin user (the "Admin" role, which has Work orders > View and Create & Edit) at {Location-A}.
    For example: {Location-A} is Staging Heavy Duty - 9919.
  • The browser window is 1440 px wide with the zoom at 100%, and the design picture "DC-05-tech-view-rows-regular-light-1440.png" attached to this case is open beside it at 100% (actual size). Names, numbers and rank numbers in the pictures are sample data.
  • Two technicians are active at {Location-A} with the "Technician" role: {Technician-A}, who has a profile photo, and {Technician-B}, who has none.
    For example: {Technician-A} is ZZAUTOTEST C590114 Eva and {Technician-B} is ZZAUTOTEST C590114 Finn.
  • Customer {Customer-A} has an Approved work order {Work-order-1}, led by {Technician-A}, with a service advisor and one approved line {Line-1} whose technician is {Technician-B}, who is clocked in to it; and an Invoiced work order {Work-order-2}, led by {Technician-A}. To make it Invoiced: create a work order like {Work-order-1} with one approved line, complete the line, then on its Finance tab click Mark Reviewed (fill Mileage or Engine Hours if the Mark as reviewed window asks, then click Confirm review) and click Create Invoice.
    For example: {Customer-A} is ZZAUTOTEST C590114 Cell Styles, {Work-order-1} and {Work-order-2} are S10043-17812 and S10043-17813, and {Line-1} is "Service - Full grease service".
  • Starting screen: "Work Orders" > "All" tab, "Tech View" shown, the name of {Customer-A} in "Search", no filter chosen, "Assigned to me" off, density "Regular".
  • If any record above is missing, mark this test Blocked: "setup not done".
custom_steps:
1. Look at the "Number" cell of the row for {Work-order-1}.
  2. Look at the "Progress" cell of the same row.
  3. Look at where the "Status", "Waiting On Parts" and "Progress" cells sit in their columns.
  4. Look at the "Service Advisor" cell.
  5. Look at the "Assigned Techs" cell.
  6. Hover the first avatar in the "Assigned Techs" cell.
  7. Look at the "Waiting On Parts", "Clocked In" and "Total price" cells.
  8. Look at the "Number" cell of the row for {Work-order-2}.
  9. Hover the small padlock next to that number.
  10. Click "List" in the display switcher.
custom_expected:
Expected results

  • Step 1: the number is blue like a link, a little darker than the blue numbers in the design picture, not black.
